gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 11 build entry now keeps the existing gpio_wdt lane, the bcm2835_wdt starter tests, and the bcm2835 survey checkpoint reviewable together so the watchdog tranche does not drift across simple-driver anchors.

A dedicated survey gate still matters after the starter lands and master advances because it keeps the remaining bcm2835_wdt gap explicit instead of letting the now-established scaffold imply platform or hardware parity that has not been implemented.

The survey note now records the current master head where the bcm2835_wdt starter, probe-time bookkeeping helper, registration summary, and remove-time ownership summary are already landed while platform registration, PM base wiring, and live poweroff-handler coordination remain out of scope.

The bounded starter now covers timeout tick encoding, running-bit detection, start and stop register transitions, restart intent, halt-partition bookkeeping, a tiny probe summary, a registration-facing handoff or poweroff ownership summary, and a remove-time ownership summary without claiming platform-backed behavior.

Dedicated Phase 11 tests now keep timeout conversion, restart intent, halt-partition bookkeeping, probe-time watchdog-core bookkeeping, registration or poweroff ownership outcomes, and remove-time poweroff ownership outcomes reviewable without pretending hardware-backed execution exists.

A dedicated slice note now documents exactly what the starter, probe summary, registration summary, and remove-time ownership summary cover and what remains out of scope so the repo does not conflate the starter with full platform or poweroff integration.

The lane now lands a tiny probe-time summary around bootloader-carried running state, heartbeat and nowayout initialization, restart priority, stop-on-reboot setup, watchdog parent linkage, and system-power-controller eligibility before any platform registration or MMIO-backed behavior.

The lane now also records registration-facing handoff and poweroff ownership outcomes so an already-running watchdog, watchdog registration intent, and poweroff claim-vs-conflict behavior remain reviewable before any live PM base wiring or watchdog-core registration.

The lane now records a tiny remove-time ownership summary for clearing the shared poweroff handler only when the bcm2835 driver currently owns it, while leaving conflicting or unrelated ownership untouched before any actual platform remove or poweroff plumbing.

Platform registration, PM base acquisition, live watchdog registration, and live poweroff-handler coordination remain blocked until the lane has the landed probe, registration, and remove summaries plus a hardware-validation matrix that can describe those side effects honestly.
